periodicity.text: The light curve is dominated by a smooth sinusoid with period 0.13850 d (Lomb-Scargle power 0.88); the adopted 0.69290 d is 5.00 x that. The true period is more likely 0.13850 d (pulsation or spots) or 0.27700 d (contact binary), and the 'eclipses' may not be eclipses.

writeup: TIC 399544063 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.6929 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse that dims the system by 3.13%, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The eclipse signal is strong, with a BLS detection significance of 947.4 and pixel-level difference imaging confirming a peak signal-to-noise of 30.3, though the centroid offset of 2.2 arcsec from the target warrants consideration. The machine learning screening score of 0.95 indicates high confidence in this as a real target. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a potentially new find. All data quality checks passed without flags, supporting the reliability of this automated detection.
